tagline.text: Nueva Valencia's signature beach, with a rocky shoreline and a cluster of resorts

location.label: Location
location.text: Coast of Barangay Alubihod, Nueva Valencia, Guimaras

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱800–3,000 (per person, day trip round trip from Iloilo including transport, lunch and a shared cottage)

children.text: Alubihod Beach is the signature beach of Nueva Valencia in Guimaras, with cream-colored sand, blue water and small resorts set among rocky shores. It makes a good base for a day trip or overnight stay from Iloilo, leading on to island hopping and lighthouse and monastery tours.

Alubihod Beach is a beach in Nueva Valencia in the southwest of Guimaras Island. Guimaras has several beaches, but the greatest number of resorts is clustered around this one, so it is the most popular choice as a base for staying on the island. One beach guide says the sand here is not the pure white of Boracay or Palawan but has a cream tint, the water glows blue, and rock formations along the shoreline make for good photos. When you go, you get the impression of a quiet neighborhood beach rather than a glamorous tourist spot.

At the beach you can swim, take photos and enjoy light activities such as beach volleyball and Frisbee. The sand is wide with plenty of room, and camping is said to be possible with permission. Admission depends on where you enter. One guide says there is usually no fee if you do not enter through a resort, while some resorts charge a small entrance fee. One blog listed about
at one resort and about
at another, so check with the resort before you go.

Alubihod is closer to a base camp for touring the whole island than a quiet retreat. Lodgings such as Raymen Beach Resort, Cabugan Adventure Resort, Jannah Glycel Beach House and Playa de Paraiso Resort are said to be clustered along the same coast. From the beach, you can hire a boat to Turtle Island, Baras Beach, Natago Beach and coral snorkeling spots, and by land you can combine Guisi Beach, Guisi Lighthouse, the Trappist Monastery and Sad Sad Falls. In other words, you can leave your bags in one place and plan each day's outing in a different direction.
This is a place to enjoy the simple atmosphere of a countryside coast rather than expect fancy facilities. It takes about
15 minutes

by boat from Iloilo City to reach the island and then you travel overland to Alubihod, so access is reasonable. It suits people who want to escape the city bustle and feel the sea breeze, people who want to tour the island tasting mangoes, and people who want a beach stay at a relatively low cost. Guimaras is close enough to Iloilo for a day trip, but because the overland ride is long, spending a night at Alubihod lets you see the west and south of the island much more comfortably.

It is not pure white sand, but cream-colored sand, blue water and rocks along the shoreline blend together. It is good for swimming during the day and for strolls and photos in the early morning or afternoon.
The wide sand is good for volleyball or Frisbee. Camping fees reportedly vary by area and permission is needed first, so ask the resort or a village manager.

items.title: Day trip
items.subtitle: From Iloilo City to the beach and island hopping

children.text: Take a pump boat from Ortiz Wharf in Iloilo City across to Jordan Wharf (about 15 minutes).
Register at the tourism office at Jordan Wharf and arrange a tricycle or van.
Arrive at Alubihod Beach, enter a resort and rent a cottage.
Swim and stroll on the beach and rest.
Have lunch at a resort or a nearby restaurant.
Hire an island-hopping boat to go around Turtle Island or Natago Beach (about 2–3 hours).
Return to Jordan Wharf and take a boat to Iloilo.
Overland travel is on country roads and can take time, so check the time of the last boat in advance.

items.title: Overnight course
items.subtitle: Base for a trip around the island

children.text: Look around the Trappist Monastery in Jordan, see the mango products and buy souvenirs.
Move to Alubihod Beach, have lunch and check in.
Visit Guisi Lighthouse and Guisi Beach by tricycle.
Stroll the beach and have dinner.
Hire an island-hopping boat to see the Taklong marine reserve and neighboring islands.
Return to Jordan Wharf and cross to Iloilo.

One guide says Cebu Pacific and Philippine Airlines operate direct flights from Manila to Iloilo International Airport (ILO). Guimaras has no airport, and there are no direct flights from Manila to Guimaras.
From the airport to Ortiz Wharf in the city, travel by taxi, shuttle van or jeepney.

The Iloilo side has more departures and is the most common route.
The beach and boat tours are the focus, so the dry season, when it is clear and the sea is calm, is best. On clear days the water looks bright blue and snorkeling visibility is good.
In the third week of April the mango festival (Manggahan Festival) is held and the island comes alive. Lodging may be crowded then, so book in advance.

Resorts are clustered along the beach, so choosing is easy. Raymen Beach Resort, Cabugan Adventure Resort, Jannah Glycel Beach House and Playa de Paraiso Resort are among those mentioned. One review says cottages at one place cost
, so compare. It is safest to confirm reservations and the latest rates directly with each resort. During the April mango festival and on weekends, book ahead.

Meals are taken at resort restaurants or small shops nearby. The choices are limited and mostly seafood and local dishes. Guimaras is famous for mangoes, so in season try fresh mangoes and mango desserts. It is easier to prepare snacks and water in Iloilo beforehand. One guide advises withdrawing enough cash in Iloilo and carrying small bills.

Bring plenty of cash and change. It may be hard to use cards in the countryside.
Put your phone and camera in waterproof pouches and bring a power bank.
If you have a picnic on the beach, take your trash with you.
Camping fees vary by area, so get permission first.
It is convenient to register first at the tourism office at Jordan Wharf and ask about fares.
For island hopping, the more people there are, the lower the cost per person, so gather a group.
Plan your schedule around the time of the last boat to Iloilo.
At Jordan Wharf, tricycle and tour operators meet passengers as they arrive, so going through the tourism office reduces fare disputes.
Even outside April, the mango season, you can buy processed mango products at the monastery and souvenir shops, so plan your gifts on the way back.
Entrance and cottage rates differ by resort, so there can be a big difference in price even on the same beach. Confirm the total before you enter.
Most of the fare information comes from blog sources dated 2015–2019. Check current prices locally. In particular, rates in 2015–2016 blogs may differ greatly from today's.
Boat service is affected by weather and waves and may be cancelled.
Parts of the beach are rocky and slippery, so be careful when walking in sandals.
There is little shade at midday, so guard against UV and heatstroke.
Many swimming areas have no lifeguards, so always watch children.
It is said to be a long way, about 24 km, from Jordan to Alubihod, and if you arrive late there may be no transport. Start early.
The island best suited to a two-day trip combining mangoes, a monastery and beaches.
The central city of Western Visayas with the airport and wharf, and the starting point for a Guimaras trip.
Ruins of a Spanish-era lighthouse, a nearby historic spot that is good to visit by tricycle.
A reserve where you can see mangroves and coral, which can be linked from the beach by boat tour.
A monastery in Jordan where you can buy monastery products such as mango jam.
